name: nml-lang
description: Syntax highlighting and language support for the NML configuration language

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In an untrusted workspace the neutral nml-lsp still validates committed and cached schema (NML is data, not code). A project's own tool language server (`<tool> lsp`) is only launched once you trust the workspace.

walkthroughs.title: Get schema-aware NML editing
walkthroughs.description: Validate NML config against its schema, with completions and hovers.

steps.title: Install the language server
steps.description:
The neutral server is `nml-lsp`. Install it on your PATH (e.g. `cargo install --locked nml-lsp`, or copy it to `~/.cargo/bin/nml-lsp`), or point `nml.server.path` at it.
[Open NML settings](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%22nml.server%22)

steps.title: Use your tool's schema (optional)
steps.description:
If your project is built with a schema-provider tool (e.g. nudge), declare it in `nml-project.nml`:

```
project MyApp:
    provider:
        tool = "nudge"
```

In a trusted workspace the editor then validates against the exact tool binary — zero sync. Otherwise the neutral server serves the tool's published package.

steps.title: Open an NML file
steps.description:
Open any `.nml` file. The status bar (bottom-right) names the active schema package and version — hover for the content hash (`blake3:{hash8}`), delivery channel, binding, and server label. Errors, completions, and hovers come from that schema.
[Open a folder](command:workbench.action.files.openFolder)

nml.server.path.description: Absolute path to the neutral nml-lsp binary (relative paths are refused). Defaults to ~/.cargo/bin/nml-lsp. Machine-scoped on purpose: a workspace cannot set it, so a repository can never redirect the language server at an untrusted binary. Paths inside an open workspace folder are refused (same RCE class as workspace-resident provider binaries).

nml.trace.server.description: Log LSP protocol messages to the NML Language Server Trace output channel. Off by default.
